Chapter 10: Honoring the Seasons—Living in Tune with Life’s Rhythms
As you move through the journey of wintering, something shifts deep inside. Suddenly, time doesn’t feel like a straight path anymore. Instead, it unfolds in seasons—each with its own challenges, and its own gifts. Have you ever felt that pressure to always be in “summer mode”—always thriving, always productive? It can be exhausting. But what if you could let go, just a little, and find a gentler rhythm?
Imagine a couple, hoping to start a family. Their journey stretched into a long season of waiting. Some days brought hope, others disappointment. And as their friends’ lives seemed to move forward, they felt left behind. But over time, they learned something important. They began to honor their own pace, to find quiet meaning in the slow days, and to trust that their story would unfold, in its own time.
Most of us want life to be predictable and under control. We resist the idea of cycles, don’t we? But here’s something to pay attention to: everyone moves through periods of growth, rest, loss, and renewal. When you accept this, it actually gets easier—not just to survive the tough times, but to really appreciate the good ones.
Think about a small business owner facing a tough season. Instead of panicking during slow months, they used that time to reflect—what really matters? Where do I want to go next? By reconnecting with their values and dreaming up new directions, they found themselves more grounded. So when things picked up again, they felt ready—aligned with their true purpose.
Honoring the seasons means letting go of the need to be “on” all the time. It’s about listening—to your body, your heart, and the world around you. Some days call for action, others for rest. And there’s real wisdom in knowing the difference.
Life’s cycles aren’t obstacles to fight against—they’re patterns to embrace. And when you live in tune with those rhythms, you’ll find it’s so much easier to move through wintering, and to welcome the return of light with gratitude.
